http://www.greekherald.com/news/27922007.text: Kiev's 'terrorist plague' spreading across Europe - Russian embassy RT.com 03 Aug 2026, 04:11 GMT+10 Investigators have yet to name any suspects behind the bombing of an Italian restaurant in central Moscow Ukraine's "terrorist plague" is spreading across Europe, the Russian Embassy in Italy has claimed, accusing Kiev of orchestrating the deadly bombing of the Balzi Rossi restaurant in central Moscow. An improvised explosive device detonated outside the Italian restaurant on Kudrinskaya Square on Saturday evening after an unidentified woman allegedly attempted to carry it inside. The security guard who stopped her at the entrance was killed in the blast, along with the courier and at least three patrons attending a private event. Almost two dozen others were injured. The National Antiterrorism Committee has not publicly identified any suspects or linked the attack to Ukraine, another state or any particular organization, while no group has claimed responsibility. In a statement on Sunday, the Russian Embassy in Italy claimed that the "bloody tentacles of Zelensky's terrorist gang" had chosen Balzi Rossi partly to frighten foreigners working in Russia. It described the "Kiev regime" as "another emanation of Al-Qaeda and Islamic State" and accused Western officials who continue to fund and arm Ukraine of enabling terrorism. "It has now become completely clear that the explosion at the Balzi Rossi restaurant and other terrorist attacks in Russia, Monaco and elsewhere show that the Ukrainian terrorist plague is already spreading across Europe, and particularly Italy," the embassy said. Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin described the explosion as a "brutal terrorist act" and vowed that those responsible would be found and punished. Similar attacks blamed on Kiev Russian officials have not announced any arrests or disclosed a suspected motive, but the embassy's allegations follow several previous bomb attacks for which Moscow explicitly blamed Ukrainian intelligence services. Russian journalist Darya Dugina was killed in August 2022 after a bomb was planted in her vehicle. Russia's Federal Security Service accused Ukrainian special services of organizing the assassination and identified Ukrainian national Natalya Vovk as the alleged perpetrator. According to the FSB, she fled to Estonia and has since vanished from public view. A bombing that killed military blogger Vladlen Tatarsky in St. Petersburg in April 2023 bore a more direct resemblance to the Balzi Rossi attack. Darya Trepova carried an explosive device disguised as a statuette into a cafe where Tatarsky was addressing an audience and presented it to him as a gift. The device exploded shortly afterwards, killing Tatarsky and injuring dozens of people. Russian investigators concluded that Trepova had acted on instructions from handlers in Ukraine. She maintained that she had been deceived and believed the statuette contained a listening device rather than a bomb, but a court convicted her of terrorism and sentenced her to 27 years in prison. Kiev never formally admitted involvement, but its former military intelligence chief, Kirill Budanov, later hinted that his agency was behind several high-profile killings inside Russia and promised to " keep killing Russians anywhere on the face of this world." Terrorism beyond Russia The June 29 bombing in Monaco cited by the embassy also involved a woman allegedly recruited by a Ukrainian military intelligence network, according to Russian law enforcement sources. In that attack, a backpack containing an improvised explosive device packed with shrapnel was placed outside a residential building and detonated remotely, injuring Ukrainian businessman Vadim Ermolaev, his partner and her 13-year-old son. The suspected courier, Anastasia Berezovskaya, fled to Ukraine before Interpol issued a Red Notice for her arrest. She was later found shot dead and buried near Kiev. Ukrainian authorities detained two men in connection with her killing, including Vitaly Zhikovich, whom Russian law enforcement sources described as a serving colonel in Ukraine's military intelligence agency. Recordings obtained by RT captured Zhikovich discussing plans to recruit unsuspecting civilians, including women and minors, to transport explosives, sometimes without knowing that they would be killed when the devices detonated. Photograph: Anonymous/Getty Images View image in fullscreen A young woman in Bukan, Iran, without a hijab during nationwide protests, September 2022. Photograph: Anonymous/Getty Images Rights and freedom Global development Iranian security forces coordinated killing, torture and sexual abuse of protesters, says Amnesty Leaked documents and testimony reveal extent of regime’s crackdown in 2022 and how it paved the way for more brutal killings of protesters this year Supported by About this content Deepa Parent Wed 16 Sep 2026 05.00 EDT Last modified on Wed 16 Sep 2026 05.01 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Iranian security forces “coordinated” the killing, torture and sexual abuse of hundreds of people who took part in the women-led nationwide protests in September 2022, according to leaked state documents and interviews. Tens of thousands of people, including children, took to the streets of towns and cities across Iran after the death in custody of Mahsa Amini, a 22-year-old Kurdish woman, after her arrest by the “morality” police for allegedly not complying with the country’s hijab regulations. In response, the Iranian state instigated a brutal crackdown. Official statements and leaked documents cited by Amnesty reveal instructions for a “firm and severe” response. One leaked order instructed forces to “respond mercilessly and go as far as causing death”. The rights group has now investigated and verified the deaths of 377 protesters and bystanders, including 56 children. It also documented the cases of 16 people who were reportedly subjected to rape while arbitrarily detained in connection with the uprising, who included six women, seven men, a 14-year-old girl and two boys aged 16 and 17. The Amnesty report said: “State agents penetrated women and girls vaginally, anally and orally, while men and boys were penetrated anally. Victims were penetrated with wooden and metal batons, glass bottles, hosepipes and/or the sexual organs and fingers of agents.” The harrowing findings echo testimonies gathered by the Guardian during and after the crackdown. In a Guardian report from December 2022 medics said security forces were shooting female protesters in the faces, breasts and genitals, and warned that the severity of the injuries could leave hundreds of young Iranians with permanent damage. View image in fullscreen An X-ray of a woman shot in the crotch during Iran protests in 2022, with about 200 metal balls embedded in her upper thigh and pelvic area. Photograph: supplied In testimony published in 2023, a 25-year-old protester told the Guardian she had been blindfolded and sexually assaulted during interrogation by security agents. Similar testimonies involving sexual assault and torture were reported by people interviewed following the anti-regime protests that took place in January 2026 . Amnesty’s report says years of impunity for the violent crackdown paved the way for the even more brutal crackdown on the nationwide anti-government protests in January 2026, which culminated in the deaths of thousands of protesters over 48 hours on 8 and 9 January. Agnès Callamard, Amnesty International’s secretary general, said: “This investigation exposes the layers of command and coordination behind the Iranian authorities’ deadly protest crackdowns. The agents on the streets operated within a hierarchical and coordinated chain of command linking them to officials who directed, enabled, facilitated and supported crimes committed on a massive scale.” skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every fortnight Sign up to Global Dispatch Get a different world view with a roundup of the best news, features, opinion and photography, curated by our global development team after newsletter promotion Amnesty identified 87 Iranian officials, including the late supreme leader Ali Khamenei, and Mohammad Bagheri, the former chief of the general staff of the armed forces, killed in an airstrike in June 2025, who it said should be investigated for “crimes against humanity”. Amnesty also named the then minister of interior, Ahmad Vahidi, who has since become the general commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, and the then deputy minister of interior for police and security, Majid Mirahmadi. The politician did not clarify whether, in her view, Russia currently poses a threat to Latvia. She said geopolitical relations should be managed through diplomacy and criticised the actions of current Foreign Minister Baiba Braže (JV), who, in Stepaņenko’s view, is escalating tensions in Latvia’s relations with other countries. Stepaņenko also declined to comment on statements about the Baltic states made by former Russian President Dmitry Medvedev, which have been widely reported by Latvian and international media. “What do I have to do with some former politicians?” Stepaņenko responded when asked about threats Medvedev has made concerning Latvia, among other countries. She added that she had nothing to do with former presidents or their statements.
